title: Tara Warned Vali
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.instagram:
Before the duel, Vali was warned. And the warning came from his queen, Tara.

Before Vali went out to fight, his queen Tara held him back: Sugriva has not come alone; his ally is Rama; make Sugriva crown prince and end the feud (Valmiki Ramayana 4.15). Vali's answer: "Rama knows dharma; how could he do wrong?" (4.16.5). As he died, Vali told Sugriva: Tara's judgement never fails (4.22.14).

Should Vali have listened to Tara?

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.youtube_description:

Before Vali went out to fight, his queen Tara held him back: Sugriva has not come alone; his ally is Rama; make Sugriva crown prince and end the feud (Valmiki Ramayana 4.15). Vali's answer: "Rama knows dharma; how could he do wrong?" (4.16.5). As he died, Vali told Sugriva: Tara's judgement never fails (4.22.14).

Should Vali have listened to Tara?

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)
Verses:
• Sugriva roared again at the gates of Kishkindha. Vali, in the inner palace, rose in anger. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.14.18; 4.15.1-4.15.5
• But one person saw the danger. Vali's queen, Tara. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.15.6
• "The brother who fled in defeat is roaring again so soon. He has not come alone." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.15.9-4.15.12
• "I have heard it from Angada. His friend is Shri Rama: the refuge of the distressed, protector of all who come to him." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.15.14-4.15.16
• "My hero, make Sugriva crown prince. Give up this feud with your brother." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.15.20-4.15.22
• "Rama knows dharma. He is grateful. How could he do a sinful thing?" — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.16.5
• Vali swore Tara back by his own life. In tears, she walked around him, chanted prayers for his victory, and went inside. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.16.8-4.16.10
• Then Rama set an arrow like a venomous serpent to his bow, and struck Vali in the chest. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.16.25
• "And Tara's judgement is never wrong. Whatever she says, do it." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.13-4.22.14
